page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by the AWS Graviton series ARMv9 architecture utilizing ARM Neoverse-V2 cores operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, providing 4 vCPUs. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core, alongside a shared 36 MB L3 cache pool. The configuration features 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached elastic block storage, and no hardware GPU acceleration is included. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across varied computational tasks. The instance yields balanced single-thread and multi-thread ratings on Geekbench (1,865 single-core and 5,917 multi-core) and stress-ng tests. In compression benchmarks, single-threaded bzip3 decompression ranks in the top 25% with 14.41 GB/sec throughput, while gzip compression achieves 30.3 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing shows steady performance with large-block uncached read speeds of 96.33 GB/sec and write speeds of 44.65 GB/sec. However, PassMark tests reveal weaknesses in vector and extended instruction sets, with the encryption test scoring in the lowest decile at 753.68. Synthetic LLM inference also demonstrates limitations, achieving 6.53 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

The 1:4 compute-to-memory distribution and dedicated physical core structure make this server efficient for routine microservices and background application processing without hyperthreading contention. Because local storage is absent, storage costs and performance depend entirely on attached EBS volumes. The instance is well matched for mid-sized relational database operations, Redis caching clusters (processing 9.54 million operations per second in testing), static web servers delivering up to 9.78 GB/sec throughput, and general enterprise containerized workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.xlarge is an ARM-based general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 vCPUs clocked at 2.8 GHz and 16.0 GB of system memory. Operating on the AWS Nitro system, it includes 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, 36 MB of L3 cache, and lacks local instance storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the middle tier for general multi-core compute, web serving (9.78 GB/sec throughput), and in-memory operations (9.54 million Redis SET operations/sec), with above-average decompression speed offset by weak extended cryptographic performance. The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory configuration delivers balanced resource density, making it suitable for distributed caching, containerized microservices, build pipelines, and general business applications.
